Fault surfaces v1 from catalog v5.1

2026-11-25 (revised after review the same day). Plane-based fault surfaces refitted on catalog v5.1 (NonLinLoc in the 3D model v0.3.1, re-timed picks), compared surface by surface with v0 (catalog v4). Code: workflow/07_faults/v1_*.py on branch analysis/v51-faults. Private working product.

Status. These products rest on catalog v5.1, which will be superseded. The PI adopted velocity model v0.4.0 (v0.3.1 re-inverted with the re-timed picks, D-B082); v0.4.1 (surface floor in the inversion, D-B083) is being built; catalog v6.0 (D-B079, NonLinLoc with SSST station terms) will replace v5.1, and the fault surfaces will be redone on v6.0. Waveform review reports for four v5.1 location problems are in /wd1/mdenolle_data/catalog_v5/v5.1_review/index.html (P1 Mount St Helens deep events, P2 Brookings 2012, P3 events with ComCat moment tensors, P4 deep-pass and far-only events); the surfaces and events they touch are flagged here.

Summary

  • 142 surfaces (99 steep, dip ≥ 45°) from 101,296 well-constrained events (v0: 141 surfaces from 76,281 events). 64,272 events (63% of the fit set) are fit members of a surface (v0: 53,291, 70%).
  • Every located event (171,719; 623 rows without a hypocentre left out) has an assignment: 64,272 fit members; 12,651 'assigned' (compatible with exactly one surface: within twice their combined uncertainty and within 10 km; this is compatibility, not location on the surface); 26,257 compatible with two or more surfaces (ambiguous); 37,468 compatible with no surface in the fitted regions; 26,874 at Axial Seamount, which was not fitted (left out as in v0), so they are neither on nor off a surface; 3,313 non-earthquakes (event_flag); 884 weekday-daytime members of surfaces removed for their timing (likely blasts). Fractions of events on or off faults must leave Axial out.
  • 'assigned' is loose. Of the 12,651 assigned events, 45% are tier D, 4,899 lie more than 5 km from the surface (median 4.0 km, against 0.71 km for fit members), 831 are floor_limited and 37 far_only (far-only events moved from near the surface in v4 to 44-64 km in v5.1; v5.1 review P4). The column on_surface_strict keeps fit members plus assigned tier A-C events within 2 km without floor_limited, far_only or deep_pass: 65,709 events.
  • Against v0 (by shared fit members): matched 50, new 39, split 23, split and merged 20, merged 10 among the v1 surfaces; of the 141 v0 surfaces: matched 50, merged 25, lost 23, split and merged 20, dispersed 13, split 10.
  • Literature: 15 v1 surfaces carry a v0 match unchanged, 88 carry one marked for re-check (split, merged or moved), and 39 are new and need a literature check (fault_surfaces_v1_literature_todo.csv).
  • Uncertainty: the surfaces depend on the detection run. sigma_total (median 0.59 km, 10th-90th percentile 0.23-1.07 km) and the strike/dip intervals hold for a fixed set of members only. The detection itself is much less certain. Over the four detection reruns of v0 (seeds, tolerance), the range of strike of the best-matching plane has a median of 103° for the 84 unstable surfaces and 6.5° for the 42 stable ones (non-strand surfaces matched in at least one rerun; the 12 strands are not rerun, and v1_MT031, v1_ON025, v1_WA002, v1_WA004 match no plane in any rerun). In the verifier's reruns, of the 130 non-strand surfaces, 38 are recovered (Jaccard ≥ 0.5) on a random 80 % of the fit set (27/42 of the 'stable' ones), 12 after moving every event once by its own catalog error (9/42 'stable'), and 10 of 116 on tiers A-B only; 9 pass both the subsample and the perturbation tests (v1_MT001, v1_ON014, v1_ON016, v1_ON021, v1_ON024, v1_OR001, v1_OR002, v1_PU006, v1_WA001). Do not use 0.59 km as the position uncertainty of a surface that fails these tests (columns recovery_*, strike_settings_range_width, flags).
Findings to read first
  • Most surfaces are not robust at the detection level. The per-surface sigmas are conditional on the member set. Rerunning the detection on a random 80 % of the fit set recovers 38 of the 130 non-strand surfaces (Jaccard ≥ 0.5); moving every event once by its own catalog error recovers 12; tiers A-B alone recover 10 of 116. Only 9 pass both the subsample and the perturbation tests (v1_MT001, v1_ON014, v1_ON016, v1_ON021, v1_ON024, v1_OR001, v1_OR002, v1_PU006, v1_WA001), and 3 pass all three. The perturbation test is pessimistic, because tier B and C errors exceed the scatter. Over the builder's four reruns the strike range has a median of 103° for the 84 unstable and 6.5° for the 42 stable surfaces (non-strand surfaces matched in at least one rerun; the 12 strands are not rerun, and v1_MT031, v1_ON025, v1_WA002, v1_WA004 match no plane in any rerun). Use a surface's geometry only where its recovery_tests and stable columns support it. There is no null test yet of how many 30-event 'planes' a catalog of the same density without faults would give.
  • Fewer events on a fault than v0, for a stated reason. 142 surfaces hold 64,272 fit members. The first v1 run, with the v0 code unchanged, found 192 planes, 75,409 of 101,296 events (74 %), but 26 of its planes ended flatter than 30° after reassignment, as 24 of v0's 141 did. With the dip rule applied in every reassignment pass, flat clouds no longer pass as faults; the share on a fault drops most in Puget (v0 61 %, v1 34 %) and onshore, where v0 kept low-dip layers (PU001, PU002, ON002).
  • Matched surfaces moved with their events. 50 v0 surfaces have one v1 counterpart. Their centroids moved a median 5.9 km horizontally and +2.3 km in depth, close to the median v4 → v5.1 depth shift of their events (+2.1 km). Strike changed by a median 23° (normals 26° apart); 17 kept their strike within 10° and 16 changed strike by more than 45° (14 have normals more than 45° apart). The other v0 surfaces: 25 merged, 10 split, 20 in mixed groups, 13 dispersed over several v1 surfaces, 23 lost; 39 v1 surfaces are new.
  • Blanco depths moved down; rectangles reach 30-50 km. The events of the v0 Blanco Ridge strand (BL003a, 3,440 events) went from a median 9.2 km (v4) to 16.5 km (v5.1). Against the Lange et al. (2026) OBS catalog, v5.1 tier A-C Blanco Ridge events are a median 2.9 km deeper with a 90th percentile of +13 km, Gorda Depression +5.6 km (+16.6 km) (catalog paired_v5.1.md). This deep tail sets the bottom of the Blanco rectangles. 4 Blanco surfaces are centred below 20 km (v1_BL009, v1_BL012, v1_BL015, v1_BL016), and one deep surface under the Cascadia Depression with only 18 depth-ok events was removed as an artefact, as v0 did for three.
  • The Cascadia Depression N-S faults are not recovered as N-S planes. The events of v0 BL005, BL008 and BL012 (N-S normal faults, high-confidence literature match) keep their N-S map elongation in v5.1 (azimuths 10°, 177°, 4°). The v1 detection first fitted a plane striking 121° and dipping 68° (2,357 events, 64 km long) through the dense cluster and on to the western Blanco Ridge (v1_BL004), then split the rest (BL005: v1_BL004 36%, v1_BL006 25%, v1_BL012 6%; BL008: v1_BL004 47%, v1_BL006 24%, v1_BL012 5%; BL012: v1_BL004 29%, v1_BL010 24%, v1_BL006 13%). This comes from the detection order, not from the relocation. A fit restricted to the Cascadia Depression is needed before v1 is used there.
  • Deep events under Mount St. Helens are probably a recurring non-earthquake signal. Surface v1x_06 (39 events at 60 km under the volcano) was removed for its timing (64% weekday daytime). In the Mount St. Helens box, 331 of 7,471 located events are deeper than 30 km (30-118 km; tiers A 1, B 3, C 118, D 209; median sig_z 17 km although stations are a few km away), and 22 of them occur on Wednesdays between 19:14 and 19:20 UTC (on Tuesdays at that time: 0). The waveform review (v5.1 review P1) found that the analog UW channels HSR, EDM and STD carry a weekly artificial signal on Wednesdays 19:14-19:21 UTC from 2011-05 to 2013-08; the deep events are 96 % UW P picks, 80 % have all P picks within 0.5 s and 73 % have no S pick. They are likely false events, pending human review. Kept surface v1_ON028 (42 events, rectangle at 22-37 km under the volcano) holds part of the same population and is flagged; the 331 deep events carry a catalog_note in the assignment file. A catalog problem, not a fault.
  • The 2012 Brookings swarm is now at about 52 km. v1_GO022 (39 events, 33 in 2012; v0 GO020, a candidate new structure at about 12 km) lies at 42-65 km in v5.1, against a median 20 km in v4; depth_quality is ok for 100% of its events, median sig_z 7 km, nearest station 45 km. Slab2 puts the slab top at a median 10 km under its events. The waveform review (v5.1 review P2) explains the depth: predicted S-P is not monotonic with depth in the v5.1 grids, so about 7-9 km and about 56 km both fit the distant stations, and NonLinLoc took the deep one. The surface and its events are flagged; its depth is not usable.
  • Endeavour-Explorer surfaces sit at 30-60 km (5 surfaces) on events whose depths the catalog marks as unconstrained (ridge regions). Their map traces can be used; their depths and dips cannot.
  • Catalog errors and scatter. Members were selected within the detection tolerance of their plane, so their residuals are truncated and the expected median |residual|/error is below 0.67: 0.67, 0.60 and 0.42 for tiers A, B and C. Observed: 0.77, 0.49 and 0.30. Tier A scatters about 15 % more than its errors allow: either the tier A errors are too small or the fault zones have a width. Tier B and C errors are larger than the scatter, by less than a comparison with 0.67 suggests. The RMS residual is 1.1-1.2 km for every tier, close to what the selection tolerance allows (about 2.3 km for vertical faults), so the zone widths are set by the method more than by the locations.
  • Surfaces whose members moved more than 10 km in depth from v4 to v5.1 are flagged (17 surfaces, on the median shift of all members or of the depth_quality ok members). In 4 of them at least half of the events are depth_quality ok and those events themselves moved more than 10 km, where the catalog gives no other warning (median shift of the depth-ok members): v1_GO022 +30.6 km, v1_ON017 +15.0 km, v1_GO004 +14.8 km, v1_GO019 +13.2 km. Flagged on all members only, with at least half depth-ok: v1_GO020 (+12.1 km for all members, +7.4 km for the 63% depth-ok), v1_GO023 (+17.3 km for all members, +8.9 km for the 65% depth-ok). The v5.1 events with ComCat moment tensors are a median 13.7 km deeper than ComCat (v5.1 review P3), so these depths are not confirmed.
  • Timing. Of the members of the 9 surfaces removed for their timing, only the weekday-daytime ones (884) are marked as likely non-earthquakes; the other 253 are assigned like any event (column removed_surface). Kept surfaces with at least twice the fit-set weekday-daytime rate are flagged: v1_MT031 (53%, binomial p 0.0003), v1_ON030 (53%, binomial p 0.0002). 4 Blanco surfaces have a small but significant excess (28%-31% against the fit-set rate, binomial p below 0.05/152 because they are large), too small to point to blasts.

Data and event selection

Fit set (PI choice of 2026-11-25): tiers A-C located by NonLinLoc, without floor_limited, far_only and deep_pass events, without ComCat explosions, quarry blasts and other non-earthquakes and without the Texada quarry_blast_likely events. Axial Seamount stays out as in v0 (published fault maps there are better). Rows are removed by the first rule that applies:

Per-event error: sigma_h = sqrt((h_min² + h_max²)/2) / 1.515 (68 % semi-axes to one sigma, the convention of the tomography code; the catalog has no ellipse azimuth) and sigma_z = sig_z. Fit-set medians: sigma_h 1.35 km, sigma_z 3.59 km; by tier A 0.71/1.17 km, B 1.19/2.37 km, C 1.90/5.47 km. Depths are km below sea level.

Method

  1. Detection: the v0 method and parameters (fault_surfaces_planes.py): sequential local RANSAC with growth, tolerance 1.5 × sqrt((1.5 km |n_h|)² + (3 km n_z)²), ≥ 30 events, planarity ≤ 0.5, dip ≥ 30°, k-planes reassignment, merging. One change: the dip rule is also applied after every reassignment pass (in v0, 24 of the 141 surfaces ended flatter than 30° after reassignment).
  2. Blanco strands (rule of split_strands.py, now automatic): steep Blanco planes within 35° of plate motion and mostly outside the Cascadia Depression box are re-searched as map-view strands in the three v0 pools (west, Blanco Ridge, Gorda Depression). Overlapping parallel strands stay apart only if Ashman's D > 2 overall and in every year where both have ≥ 15 events; pairs whose depth offset would need a single fault dipping ≥ 60° are merged (offset follows depth, the reason v0 merged its two 'deeper band' strands).
  3. Rectangles as v0 (2-98 % extent along strike and dip + 0.5 km, plane or gentle quadratic by BIC, 1 km mesh).
  4. Uncertainty per surface: bootstrap of the members (100 draws), location Monte Carlo moving every member by its own catalog error (100 draws; v0 used nominal 1.5/1.5/3 km), model choice, combined; strike/dip intervals from each; centroid spread; stability over the four detection reruns of v0 (Jaccard overlap). These intervals are conditional on the member set. The spread of the detection itself is given separately: strike/dip range of the best-matching plane over the four reruns, and recovery (Jaccard ≥ 0.5) in three detection reruns made by the verifier of this piece (80 % subsample, every event moved once by its own error, tiers A-B only; work/verifier_reruns/).
  5. Screening: surfaces with ≥ 60 % of their events on weekdays 08-17 local time are removed (quarry blasts or other non-earthquake signals; catalog average 28 %); Blanco surfaces centred deeper than 25 km with fewer than 30 depth-ok events are removed as deep artefacts (v0 removed three such surfaces after its literature check); a final dip < 30° would also remove a surface (none left after the dip rule in detection). Of the members of a surface removed for its timing, only those on weekdays 08-17 local time are marked as likely non-earthquakes; the others are assigned like any event (column removed_surface keeps the link). Kept surfaces with at least twice the fit-set weekday-daytime rate are flagged.
  6. Assignment of every located event: distance d to the surface (offset normal to the fitted surface at the nearest point of the rectangle, plus the in-plane distance outside it); z = d / sqrt(s_e² + s_s² + W²) with s_e the event's error along that direction, s_s the surface's median sigma_total and W its zone width once the member errors are taken out. Compatible: z ≤ 2 and d ≤ 10 km. Assigned: exactly one compatible surface (compatibility, not location on it); ambiguous: two or more; none: no compatible surface; Axial Seamount events: not fitted. on_surface_strict: fit members and assigned tier A-C events within 2 km, without floor_limited, far_only or deep_pass.
  7. Comparison with v0: v0 members (catalog v4 IDs, the same as v5.1 IDs) against v1 fit members. A v0 and a v1 surface are linked when they share ≥ 15 events and these are ≥ 50 % of the v0 surface's re-found events, or ≥ 50 % of the v1 surface's events that were on a v0 surface, or ≥ 30 % of both. Connected groups: matched (1-1), split (1-n), merged (n-1), split and merged, new, lost. Removed v1 surfaces take part in the links, so a v0 surface whose events now form a removed surface is reported as lost with that reason. Literature is carried unchanged only for matched surfaces whose normals are within 25°, centroids within 10 km horizontally and within 5 km in depth; every other carried match is marked for re-check.

Blanco strands

12 strands replace 21 Blanco planes. 8 overlapping pairs were merged because their depth offset would need a single fault dipping 62-80° (the Blanco faults are near vertical, so the offset is read as depth-dependent location error, as for v0's 'deeper band' strands), and 2 because the separation failed in at least one year. Without the depth rule, v1 would keep more parallel strands; the table lists every merge.

Two Blanco Ridge strands south of the main strand v1_BL005, v1_BL009 (877 events, 32% depth-ok, centroid 23 km), v1_BL015 (257 events, 25% depth-ok, centroid 23 km), pass the depth test because the test uses depth-ok events only, which sit at the same median depth as v1_BL005. Most of their events have unconstrained depths. They are where v0's merged 'deeper band' was, and need the same check before being read as separate faults.

Strand dips (88-90°) and their 68 % intervals (about 0.2° wide) are set by the map-view band selection (events within 1.5 km of a line), not measured: the band forces a near-vertical fit. This is inherited from v0. Every strand carries a flag saying so; read their dips as 'steep', not as a measurement.

Uncertainties

Per surface (1 sigma normal to the surface, median over vertices): sigma_total 0.59 km (10th-90th percentile 0.23-1.07), of which location Monte Carlo 0.46, bootstrap 0.21 and model choice 0.16 km. The location term uses the catalog errors, which for tiers B and C are larger than the scatter, so it is an upper bound. It treats errors as independent between events; errors shared by nearby events (velocity model, station terms) move a whole surface and are not in it; the v0 → v1 shift of matched surfaces (median 5.9 km horizontally) shows their size between two location runs. Strike and dip: bootstrap 68 % interval widths, median 2.0° and 3.1°; with the location Monte Carlo 5.7° and 7.0°. Centroid: 0.72 km horizontally and 0.31 km in depth (bootstrap). 49 of 142 surfaces are stable (median Jaccard ≥ 0.5 over the four detection reruns; v0: 50 of 141).

These sigmas and intervals hold for a fixed set of members. They do not include the choice of members made by the detection, which dominates: over the four detection reruns the strike of the best-matching plane ranges over a median 103° (dip 22°) for the 84 unstable surfaces and 6.5° (dip 8.0°) for the 42 stable ones (non-strand surfaces matched in at least one rerun; the 12 strands are not rerun, and v1_MT031, v1_ON025, v1_WA002, v1_WA004 match no plane in any rerun). Checks and limits

  • 14 surfaces have mesh vertices above the ground or seafloor (GMT earth_relief 01m): the rectangle is extrapolated 0.5 km and to the 2-98 % extent of the members; no hypocentre is above the surface (catalog v5.1). Listed in the summary (n_vertices_above_surface).
  • 37 surfaces have fewer than half of their events with depth_quality ok (Blanco outside the 2012-13 OBS deployment, Gorda far from stations): their dips and depth extents rest on poorly constrained depths; dip_depth_ok and events_depth_ok_2pct_km/98pct_km give the same from the ok events only.
  • Rectangles are crude: one plane or gentle quadratic over the 2-98 % extent of the members. Curved or branching faults come out as several rectangles.
  • No relative relocation: the scatter about the surfaces (RMS about 1.2 km) is still wider than double-difference catalogs show for the same faults.
  • ComCat focal mechanisms were not used to steer or check the surfaces (PI rule).
  • The mesh vertex elevations (surface_elev_km) use GMT earth_relief 01m, not the merged GMRT surface of the catalog.

Proposed decisions

  1. Dip rule in every reassignment pass (v1_detect.reassign_dip): a plane flatter than 30° after reassignment is dropped and its events go back to the other planes. v0 checked the dip only at detection and merging; 24 of its 141 surfaces ended flatter. Effect on v5.1: 192 → 161 planes, 74 % → 67 % of the fit set on a plane. Cost: by design, faults flatter than 30° cannot be represented. Of v0's 24 surfaces flatter than 30°: 7 merged, 6 matched, 4 dispersed, 3 split and merged, 3 lost, 1 split. Among them, MT010 (12°, 774 events, medium-high confidence: 1992 Mw 7.2 Cape Mendocino / 1991 M6.0 Honeydew low-angle thrust zone) is dispersed over v1_MT007 16%, v1_MT001 15%, v1_MT003 14%; PU016 (21°, 79 events, medium confidence: Olympia structure, SE end) is lost; PU021 (20°, 62 events, low confidence: Shallow LRF / Langford area) is lost. A low-angle thrust such as the 1992 Cape Mendocino / Honeydew zone needs another method (for example a fit without the dip rule restricted to that zone).
  2. Event selection: 'deep-pass-only' read as deep_pass = True (83 tier A-C events); anss_other_event and anss_sonic_boom also excluded as non-earthquakes (1 event); Axial left out as in v0; the 2 loc_source comcat rows (tier U) are assigned with nominal errors of 1.5 km (horizontal) and 3 km (depth).
  3. Per-event error: sigma_h = sqrt((h_min² + h_max²)/2) / 1.515, isotropic (no ellipse azimuth in the catalog); sigma_z = sig_z.
  4. Blanco strands made automatic: parents are steep Blanco planes within 35° of 111° with under half of their events in the Cascadia Depression box (-128.82 to -128.60 E, 43.74 to 43.88 N); events in that box are kept out of the strand pools; per-year Ashman D test (2 merges); pairs merged when their depth-ok median depths would need a single fault dipping ≥ 60° (8 merges; v0 merged two such pairs by judgement).
  5. Screening: surfaces with ≥ 60 % of events on weekdays 08-17 local time removed (9, 1,137 events; their 884 weekday-daytime events are marked as likely non-earthquakes and never assigned, the others are assigned like any event); Blanco surfaces centred deeper than 25 km with < 30 depth-ok events removed as deep artefacts (1). Kept surfaces with at least twice the fit-set weekday-daytime rate are flagged, with the binomial p. The 60 % cut is a judgement; all 9 removed surfaces have binomial p ≤ 3e-7 against the fit-set rate.
  6. Assignment: compatible when z = d / sqrt(s_e² + s_s² + W²) ≤ 2 and d ≤ 10 km; assigned only when exactly one surface is compatible, otherwise 'ambiguous' with the two nearest listed. Without the 10 km cap and the uniqueness condition, events with errors of 10-15 km were 'compatible' with surfaces up to 70 km away. 'assigned' means compatible with one surface, not located on it; on_surface_strict (fit members and assigned tier A-C events within 2 km, without floor_limited, far_only or deep_pass) is the default for counting events on faults. Axial events are 'not fitted'.
  7. v0 comparison: link when ≥ 15 shared fit members that are ≥ 50 % of either side, or ≥ 30 % of both; literature carried unchanged only for matched surfaces with normals within 25°, centroids within 10 km horizontally and within 5 km in depth; all other carried matches marked 're-check'.
  8. Flags for catalog problems on the surfaces (summary, rectangles and mesh): Mount St Helens deep population (centroid in the review box and deeper than 20 km, or ≥ 25 % of members deeper than 30 km), 2012 Brookings swarm, members moved > 10 km in depth from v4 to v5.1, weekday-daytime excess, strand dips set by the band selection, detection-level recovery.
  9. Surface IDs: v1_<region><nnn> (v0 region boxes, numbered by size); removed surfaces v1x_nn.
  10. Not done here, proposed as next steps (on catalog v6.0, which will supersede v5.1): a null test of the detection (the same detection on a spatially randomised catalog of the same density, to count the 30-event 'planes' density alone gives); a fit restricted to the Cascadia Depression; a check of v1_BL009/v1_BL015 against the OBS-era depths; a separate treatment of low-angle zones. The Mount St Helens deep events and the Brookings swarm depth are now in the v5.1 review (P1, P2).

Files

In the worktree, data/catalog_v5/v5.1_analysis/faults/: fault_surfaces_v1_summary.csv (parameters, flags, carried literature), _uncertainty.csv, _rectangles.geojson (four corners per surface), _members.csv (fit members), _assignment.csv.gz (every located event), _assignment_by_region.csv, _selection.csv, _removed.csv and _removed_members.csv, _strand_separation.csv, _strand_merges.csv, _traces.csv, _v0_pairs.csv (every linked v0-v1 pair), _v0_status.csv (every v0 surface), _v0_comparison.csv (every v1 surface, with literature), _literature_todo.csv (new surfaces), the PNG figures and this report. On /wd1/mdenolle_data/catalog_v5/v5.1_analysis/faults/: fault_surfaces_v1.geojson (1 km triangle mesh, CRESCENT CFM layout), _vertices.csv.gz (per-vertex sigmas), _ensemble.csv.gz (100 draws per vertex), _assignment.csv.gz, work/ (detection runs, logs, member residuals; work/verifier_reruns/: the verifier's three detection reruns used for the recovery columns) and RESUME.md. New columns after review: summary strike_settings_range_width, dip_settings_range_width, recovery_J_sub80, recovery_J_perturbed, recovery_J_tierAB, recovery_tests, median_shift_z_depth_ok_km, weekday_daytime_p; assignment on_surface_strict, weekday_daytime, removed_surface, catalog_note.
